Both implementations are declared inside the fragment, so the dispatch has exactly two realizable targets and the construction fixes which one. Witness: the frozen program prints a.

A declaration named `listOf` in the fragment's own package shadows the default-imported kotlin.collections.listOf (Kotlin language specification 2.x, 'Overload resolution'), so the span's resource behaviour and which element is at position 0 differ: the list may be shared rather than freshly allocated, may reorder or drop elements, and `get` may fail. Materially different on dimensions 3, 6 and 9. Witness: `fun <T> listOf(vararg e: T): List<T> = java.util.Collections.singletonList(e[1])` in the same package leaves the fragment byte-identical and makes it print b.
